strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Prevents headless run-control from reporting completion unless latest aggregate progress and terminal task/run evidence prove the run is truly closed.
Binds top-level headless closure to terminal task.run completion evidence instead of terminal status counts alone.
Keeps completion authority in the Rust runtime and prevents VSIX or caller-supplied route metadata from deciding final completion.
Uses bounded terminal completion fingerprints from run ledger evidence and keeps raw prompts, output, paths, and file content out of closure/finalization payloads.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, with supporting progress for agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: A headless drive completion closure can report Complete only after the runtime sees all tasks completed, no remaining route/runnable/in-progress work, and bounded terminal completion evidence from the latest completed task/run.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing closure logic could derive Complete from terminal status counts alone and did not require latest completion evidence, so manually terminal or failed/cancelled terminal scopes could look closed to a headless caller.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could continue expanding capabilities while still risking false Complete and premature finalization in the central autonomous development loop.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M43-M45 are Mode Pack lifecycle phases; R4.1 is P0 completion correctness remediation that changes headless closure behavior rather than adding another route or registry capability.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The implementation modifies existing headless run-control closure/finalization behavior and adds no JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. No report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, or preview surface is added; existing closure evidence remains bounded.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime now denies Complete when latest progress is stale/in-progress, when explicit routes remain, when terminal evidence is missing, or when terminal scope contains failed/cancelled tasks.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can stop or request finalization only when runtime-owned closure evidence proves the run is truly closed, which is a prerequisite for Golden Journey correctness.
answers.milestone_progress: R4.1 starts P0 completion remediation and prepares R4.2 finalization ownership binding.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: R4.1 updates the deterministic current phase manifest and archives the R4.1 value gate. Review must confirm this is P0 headless completion correctness remediation, not a wrapper or Mode Pack detour.

exit_criteria: headless completion closure Complete requires all known tasks to be Completed, not Failed or Cancelled
Complete requires no running, created, queued, runnable, or explicit route work remaining
Complete requires bounded terminal completion evidence from the latest completed task/run ledger
stale progress and in-progress task statuses take precedence over Complete
completion finalization remains denied for non-complete closure status
focused Rust tests prove true complete, missing terminal evidence denial, and failed terminal scope denial
no new RPC, report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, or preview surface is added
no raw prompts, provider responses, file content, stdout/stderr, commands, environment values, absolute paths, canonical paths, raw ledger payloads, or secrets are persisted or returned

p0_preemption_rule.effect: New non-remediation capability phases such as M45.1 remain superseded while P0 completion/security blockers are open.
